questions.q: What does an options contract give its buyer?
a: The right, but not the obligation, to trade a stock at a set price later
A guaranteed share of ownership in the underlying company
A promise that the stock price will rise before expiration
An automatic loan from the broker to cover any losses
questions.why: Lesson 1 defines an option as a contract granting the right to buy or sell at a predetermined price, if you choose.

questions.q: Why can options trading require less money than buying stock outright?
a: You pay a premium to control many shares rather than their full price
Brokers waive all fees for beginner options traders
Options never lose value, so the deposit is returned
You only pay once the trade has become profitable
questions.why: Lesson 1 notes that a small premium can control 100 shares, so less capital is needed to start.

questions.q: What is the Test Trading Strategy?
a: Practicing with virtual money in a simulator before risking real cash
Buying one share of every stock on a watch list
Testing a broker’s platform for a free trial period
Placing tiny real trades to measure your emotional response
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes using virtual trading tools as a risk-free way to practice buying and selling.

questions.q: What should you put on your watch list while test trading?
a: Major market indexes plus actively traded stocks priced at least $50
Only cheap penny stocks that could rise quickly
A single company you already know very well
Stocks chosen by your broker without your input
questions.why: Lesson 2 recommends adding SPY, QQQ, the Dow and the S&P 500, then active stocks of at least $50 per share.

questions.q: What should you do if the gap between a stock’s bid and ask price is too wide?
a: Choose a different stock with a narrower spread
Place a market order to guarantee you get in
Wait for the spread to widen even further
Buy more contracts to average out the cost
questions.why: Lesson 3 warns that a wide bid-ask spread makes profit too hard and says to find another stock.
